column1: # ⛔⭐ 91 ROWS ARRIVED HERE FROM UNGRADABLE.tsv ON 2026-09-09 (hq_P, ceo CEO-452), AND THE REASON IS THE MOST
# EXPENSIVE KIND OF INSTRUMENT ERROR: they were classed ORACLE_REFUSES, and the oracle does not refuse them.
# icont resolves `link` through the IPATH environment variable; cut without it, every progs/ program that
# links a procs/ helper -- which is this library's NORMAL SHAPE -- fails to compile, and that failure was
# recorded as the oracle's verdict on the program. Re-asked with IPATH set, 91 of the 92 compile. The one
# that still refuses is progs/qei.icn, whose reason was hand-re-measured the same morning; it stays put.
# ⛔ AND "IT STAYS PUT" LASTED ONE DAY -- qei JOINED THEM 2026-09-10, one row below, by the SAME defect wearing
# the other face. The 91 were re-asked of the oracle with the environment fixed; qei was re-asked correctly and
# still refused, so the row read as confirmed -- but nobody asked the oracle the OTHER question, whether the
# file it refused was the file upstream ships. It is not: ours carries our conversion's semicolons and upstream
# compiles rc=0. ⭐ A RE-MEASUREMENT THAT REPEATS THE ORIGINAL QUESTION CAN ONLY EVER CONFIRM; the control that
# breaks the tie is a DIFFERENT question (diff against upstream), which is the same lesson as the `-I` control
# two paragraphs down, one level up.
# ⛔ THE DIRECTION IS WHAT MAKES IT SERIOUS: an over-broad ORACLE_REFUSES moves OUR reds out of the
# denominator under the oracle's name, which is exactly the failure the POPULATION LAW exists to prevent.
# 26 of the 91 run CLEAN under a bare driver and 5 of those already produce output -- there is ground truth
# for them today. Every class below is measured, never inferred: compiled with IPATH in a staged copy, run
# once with /dev/null on stdin and a 20s cap, and bucketed by what the oracle actually did.
# ⭐ AND THE AUDIT'S FIRST ATTEMPT WAS ITSELF WRONG IN THE SAME WAY, which is why the positive control is
# not optional: it passed `-I` to icont, which has no such option, so all 92 rows "confirmed" -- confirming
# only the bad flag. Three known-good programs run through the same invocation caught it in one command.
# ⭐ SOME OF THESE WILL COME BACK, AND THAT IS THE WORK RATHER THAN A DEFECT OF THIS MOVE: `bj` wants a
# terminal ("/bin/stty: 'standard input': Inappropriate ioctl for device"), `crypt` prompts for a password,
# `applyfnc` and `comfiles` want arguments. Those end in UNGRADABLE again under a MEASURED class -- and the
# difference that matters is that somebody will have looked. UNGRADED is where a row waits for a ruling;
# ORACLE_REFUSES was a ruling nobody had made.
# ⛔ WHAT I DID **NOT** RECLASSIFY, because the probe cannot see it: the 8 NONDETERMINISTIC rows still in
# UNGRADABLE.tsv. Seven of them give byte-identical output twice one second apart -- and that proves
# nothing, because `daystil` is date-dependent and `htget` fetches over the network. The package header's
# own rule (two runs ONE SECOND APART, from env.icn) catches SECOND-resolution clock dependence and is
# blind to DAY-resolution and to the network. A probe that answers a narrower question than the reader
# thinks it asked is the same shape as the `-I` error above, one level up, so those rows stay as they are.
